CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing a continued moderate improvement in his symptoms since the last visit. He reports that his tension-type headaches have remained stable, occurring approximately once a week, with an intensity rating of 2 out of 10. He attributes this stability to the ongoing use of topiramate and amitriptyline, which he continues to tolerate well, with no significant side effects reported.
Sleep quality has remained consistent, with Mr. Smith averaging 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night. He mentions that the addition of gabapentin at bedtime has contributed positively, allowing him to fall asleep more quickly and experience fewer nocturnal awakenings. However, he still encounters sporadic sleep disruptions, primarily related to work-related stressors. He has begun practicing mindfulness meditation and deep-breathing exercises as relaxation techniques, which he finds beneficial.
Regarding persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith reports that while morning fatigue still lingers, his energy levels have improved slightly during the day, likely due to his regular exercise routine, which includes running and yoga. He denies experiencing new symptoms such as dizziness, changes in appetite, or significant weight fluctuations.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 100 mg at bedtime (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and has implemented effective stress management techniques in his daily routine. He remains physically active, participating in running and yoga, which he believes significantly enhance his mood and energy. His diet continues to be well-balanced, and he abstains from alcohol while maintaining a low caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; sleep quality consistent; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Mild fatigue persists, with no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 116/72 mmHg, HR 66 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-groomed; mood appears stable with mild anxiety noted. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no dizziness reported. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with no signs of distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Monitor for any changes in anxiety levels. Lorazepam usage remains as needed for acute episodes. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone and melatonin; gabapentin at bedtime continues to be effective; monitor for any adverse effects or further sleep disturbances. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 100 mg daily; headache frequency and intensity remain stable. Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly. Schedule a follow-up in one month to reassess treatment efficacy. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued participation in regular physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue persists or worsens, further evaluation for underlying causes will be considered.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-08-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate treatment efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to maintain a headache diary and continue tracking sleep patterns to identify potential triggers and enhance management strategies.
